newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber close mostly down on weaker cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber close mostly down on weaker cash.

text.p: CME lumber futures resumed their downtrend after short covering lacked followthrough, with concern over cash markets and weak technicals continuing to weigh on prices, traders said.
Lumber closed $5.00 per tbf lower to $0.20 higher with March off most at $385.00 and May off $0.20 at $379.30.

Short covering that developed after the initial sharp break lacked followthrough interest because of continued talk about an easier tone to cash lumber. Concern over possible heavy deliveries against the March contract added to losses, they said.
"There's been no retail demand" for lumber, one trader said citing reports of wholesalers offering cash spruce well under current mill asking prices.
Cash sources said wholesalers were offering spruce at $380 to $390 while mills kept asking prices around $414, the last official cash quote.
Short covering early filled a gap left on the chart but technicals were very weak. March penetrated a chart line and posted a two-month low of $383.00 on the early setback, chartists added.
